facts.quote: Teaching vignette (invented): five H&E slides of sentinel lymph node tissue from one patient, as released in the public CAMELYON17 data set. The data set labels each slide as one node by its largest focus, so call each slide as one node even if it shows more than one profile of nodal tissue. No immunohistochemistry, deeper levels, primary tumour, gross description or clinical history exists for these slides; this vignette is invented for teaching and carries no patient information. Review every node, call each one, and stage the set under CAMELYON17's simplified rules.
facts.basis: Invented for teaching (D13, §15.2): one generic text for all ten cases, labelled "Teaching vignette (invented)"; CAMELYON17 publishes no clinical record (FACTS §0). Its one dataset claim, one slide = one node, is S0.1 in common.facts.json.

facts.quote: Five slides, one node each by the data set's convention. Open every node, call each one, then fill the practice report.
facts.basis: The data set's one-slide-one-node convention (S0.1, common.facts.json); the rest is instruction.

facts.quote: Reference pN: pN1mi under CAMELYON17's simplified rules (2 nodes with micro- or macrometastasis). The largest annotated deposit is in node 4.
facts.basis: stages.csv (sha256 1bf47c5c3b20…) patient row patient_046.zip = pN1mi; derivePn of the node labels ['negative', 'negative', 'negative', 'micro', 'micro'] gives pN1mi (the rules reproduce stages.csv for 100 of 100 patients, FACTS §4.1, §4.2); counts macro 0, micro 2, ITC 0, positive 2. Largest annotated deposit: node 4 (1126.5 µm).

facts.quote: Two micrometastases and no macrometastasis: pN1mi, whatever the number of micro nodes.
facts.basis: stages.csv: nodes 3 and 4 micro, no macro, pN1mi; derivePn (§6.1): pN1mi whatever the number of micro nodes.

facts.quote: Node 5: labelled micrometastasis by CAMELYON17 although no single annotated focus reaches 0.2 mm (78 small foci, the largest about 190 µm; foci within 100 µm of each other span about 780 µm). AJCC also classes a deposit of more than 200 cells in one cross-section as a micrometastasis, which an outline cannot show. Calling this node ITC is a defensible disagreement.
facts.basis: §15.3 borderline caveat (PE-3, D33; FACTS §4.4): the node is labelled micro in stages.csv while its largest polygon is under 0.2 mm; AJCC 8th edition also defines a micrometastasis by > 200 cells in one cross-section, which an outline cannot show. Numbers from the committed overlay at this slide's MPP.
